title: Personalization Without Stereotyping: Do Speech LLMs Know When to Turn a Deaf Ear?
abstract: arXiv:2610.13550v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent speech LLMs can leverage rich paralinguistic cues, enabling more complex and personalized interactions. However, little work investigates how this sensitivity can lead to stereotyping, and existing evaluations largely measure demographic disparities without distinguishing beneficial personalization from stereotypical behavior. We introduce BASIS-Bench, a benchmark designed to disentangle these two aspects through three axes: (1) demographic robustness, measuring disparities in content-based tasks across speakers and demographic classification capabilities; (2) stereotypical bias, measuring whether perceived demographic cues trigger unprompted stereotypical behavior; and (3) personalization, measuring whether models can tailor responses to demographic characteristics when explicitly requested. We evaluate eight recent speech LLMs and find that, despite often recognizing demographic cues, most fail to translate them into appropriate

translated_title: 个性化而不刻板印象：语音大语言模型知道何时该“充耳不闻”吗？
translated_abstract: 近期的语音大语言模型（Speech LLM）能够利用丰富的副语言线索，实现更复杂和个性化的交互。然而，很少有研究调查这种敏感性如何导致刻板印象行为，且现有评估大多仅衡量人口统计差异，未能区分有益的个性化与刻板印象行为。我们提出了 BASIS-Bench，这是一个旨在通过三个维度区分这两个方面的基准：（1）人口统计稳健性，衡量基于内容的任务在不同说话人之间的表现差异以及人口统计分类能力；（2）刻板印象偏见，衡量感知到的人口统计线索是否会触发未经提示的刻板印象行为；（3）个性化，衡量模型在被明确要求时能否根据人口统计特征定制响应。我们评估了八个近期的语音大语言模型，发现尽管它们通常能够识别人口统计线索，但大多数模型未能将其转化为恰当的行为。
tldr: 提出了 BASIS-Bench 基准，通过人口统计稳健性、刻板印象偏见和个性化三个维度区分语音大语言模型的有益个性化与刻板印象行为，评估发现多数模型虽能识别人口统计线索却未能恰当运用。
en_tdlr: We introduce BASIS-Bench, a benchmark that disentangles beneficial personalization from stereotypical behavior in speech LLMs along three axes (demographic robustness, stereotypical bias, and personalization), finding that most models recognize demographic cues but fail to act on them appropriately.
